propositions: The test walks 884 renderable units with ~1768 serial pandoc spawns in a single monolithic test function, causing unbounded cost that crosses the 300s per-test timeout on contended macOS runners.

pytest-timeout with --timeout-method=thread kills the xdist worker process with os._exit(1) instead of failing the test, producing no traceback and reporting a worker crash rather than a test failure.
The test's cost is load-dependent, measuring 91.6s idle and 504.8s under CPU saturation (1.7x past the 300s guard), which is why only the macOS cell reds while ubuntu cells pass.
The fix chunks the equivalence comparison into fixed-size batches using pytest.mark.parametrize with _EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK constant, bounding per-test cost independently of corpus growth.
A new coverage guard test asserts that all chunks concatenate to _renderable_units() and total >= 100, preventing silent unit loss from chunking.
All 884 units remain compared against the oracle with real pandoc at _EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE 1, preserving the byte-identity property the test protects.
